title: The Moral-First Chain

canonical_node.axiom: The Good exists, underived, and is the foundation from which all else is derived downward.
definitions: The Good: the underived, postulated ultimate source, personal in nature.
Coherence: the structural form of the Good; alignment with what is, was, and will be.
Projection: the physical world as a shadow cast by the moral structure.
Measurement: the registration of coherence-condition when the projection meets a witness.
M-series: the postulate stack M0-M5 replacing bottom-up bridges.
derivation: M0 postulates the Good as underived.
M1 defines coherence as the structural form of the Good.
M2 derives the physical as a projection of the moral structure.
M3 interprets sciences as domain vocabularies of the projection.
M5 postulates the personal nature of the source.
canonical_node.action: Adopt the M-series postulate stack as the working orientation for the framework, deriving all subsequent theorems downward from M0.
boundary: Does not claim the postulates are proven results.
Does not dissolve the is-ought gap as a formal proof; it is a reframing.
Does not resolve the problem of evil; it sharpens it.
Does not claim the postulates are minimal; minimality is abductive and open.
test: Check that all derived theorems are labeled as theorems of the moral-first system, not conditional on borrowed bundles.
Verify that the four kernel assumptions are treated as postulates, not mid-chain debts.
Ensure that any counterexample to the projection grammar is preserved as a finding.
Confirm that the two soft spots (universal-cost premise, deliberative vs. moral ought) are stated as falsification criteria.

dg1_dependencies: Existing Lean kernel theorems (17 theorems, zero sorry)
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a top-down derivation order that eliminates the need for bridges between physics, morals, and God, allowing theorems to carry stronger labels.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the 17 kernel theorems and the irreducibility result (dual_substrates_from_irreducible_distinctions).
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without the M-series, the framework reverts to bottom-up with permanent construction sites (is-ought gap, bridge defenses), weakening theorem labels.

overstatement_risks: Claiming the is-ought gap is dissolved when it is only reframed.
Treating the postulates as proven results.
Assuming the projection grammar applies universally without counterexample.
Overstating the minimality of the five postulates.
kill_conditions: A counterexample to the projection grammar is found and not preserved.
The universal-cost premise is shown to be false.
The deliberative vs. moral ought distinction collapses.
The postulates are shown to be inconsistent with the kernel theorems.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the M-series as a postulate stack in Lean, with the kernel theorems as theorems of the system.

plain_summary: This sheet proposes a top-down orientation for the framework: postulate the Good (M0) and derive everything else downward, replacing bottom-up bridges. It is a working direction, not a proven result. The document claims this makes proofs easier and dissolves old problems, but those claims are not formally established.
